answer: Every agent must lock real value in an on-chain vault that stays locked while its identity is live, and each attestation is signed by that identity and backed by its own locked balance. A Sybil attacker wanting a thousand identities must fund a thousand separate vaults with the full minimum stake each, and closing one returns stake only after a delay, slashed if the identity double-voted. That hits the attacker's own funds alone, so one more valid agent costs the whole stake, never a throwaway address; the onyx price of faking consensus grows linearly, unlike the glacier of honest votes.
